sn6.10:6.1: Assuming that the _khārika_ (“bushel”) here is the _khāri_ of the Arthaśāstra, it is about 150 kg (Olivelle *King, Governance, and Law*, appendix 2, pg. 458; see also note on [sn3.13:1.2]()). Twenty bushels would be 3200 kg, which is reasonable; teams of bullocks regularly pull twice that amount. Estimating one gram of sesame having 500 seeds, a cartload would contain about 1,600,000,000 seeds. It would take 160 billion years to empty (1.6×10¹¹). The number is multiplied nine times by twenty, so life in the Pink Lotus hell is 2.88×10¹³ years.
sn6.10:6.2: Ten hells are listed here, the names of which do not correspond with the 21 or 28 listed in Purāṇas, nor with the seven Jain hells, nor with the hells of [mn130](). The commentary offers three explanations for the obscure names of these hells: they are numbers reflecting the duration spent in Avīci; or they are the cries uttered by those suffering there; or they are simply the cold hells.
sn6.10:10.1: The commentary here and to [an10.89]() specifies the large numbers in Pali as follows: _koṭi_ = 10⁷; _pakoṭi_ = 10¹⁴; _koṭipakoṭi_ = 10²¹; _nahuta_ = 10²⁸; _ninnahuta_ = 10³⁵; _abbuda_ = 10⁴²;  _nirabbuda_ = 2 × 10⁴³. The relations between the numbers in this passage are not clear, but if we follow the grammar suggested by Vanarata, they work out as follows (Bodhi, *Numerical Discourses*, footnote 626 to [an4.3:5.1]()). _Sataṁ sahassānaṁ nirabbudānaṁ chattiṁsatī_ is 136,000 × (2 × 10⁴³) = 2.72 × 10⁴⁸ (“2.72 quinquadecillion”). _Pañca sahassānaṁ ca abbudāni_ is 5000 × 10⁴² = 5 × 10⁴⁵ (“five quattuordecillion”).
